subject: Post-call: Shopline ranking pilot — model recommendations & A/B plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Walsh <emma.walsh@shopline.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-20T15:11:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Shopline ranking pilot — model recommendations & A/B plan

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary from the call
- Current setup: BM25 + light feature scoring (clicks/impressions).
- Primary objective: improve top-10 precision for product search (mobile web + app), reduce zero-click sessions, and increase conversions for category-level queries.
- Constraints: 99th-percentile latency budget must stay <= 220ms on p95 search path, and Shopline requires search query log retention controls (GDPR).

Redwood recommendation (short list)
1) First-pass: keep your existing BM25 / lexical layer as-is for recall.
2) Reranker (cross-encoder) candidate: roberta-crossenc-large-v2 (open checkpoint) OR redwood-rerank-1.0 (optimized quantized variant).
   - Why: cross-encoders provide much higher relevance at top ranks for intent-heavy queries in our evals.
3) Fallback plan: if p95 latency goes > 250ms for a segment, route that traffic to a lighter model (distil-crossenc-1.0) or increase caching for popular prefixes.

Benchmarks we ran (sampled 5k production-like queries)
- Baseline (BM25 + current features): NDCG@10 = 0.62, MRR = 0.45
- Add roberta-crossenc-large-v2 reranker (re-score top 50): NDCG@10 = 0.78 (+0.16), MRR = 0.61 (+0.16)
- redwood-rerank-1.0 (quantized) rescore top 50: NDCG@10 = 0.75, MRR = 0.59
- Latency (median / p95) for reranker on our dedicated GPUs: 12ms / 130ms per request for batched rescore(50) when batched; single-request tail can reach 220ms in worst-case.

Artifacts attached
- shopline_rerank_eval_summary.pdf (high-level results + plots)
- eval_queries_5k.csv (query sample + labels) — small extract for quick triage

Suggested pilot A/B (50/50)
- Control: current production pipeline
- Variant: same first-pass, + redwood-rerank-1.0 rescore top-50 (start with 10% traffic to validate, then 50%)
- Metrics: NDCG@10, MRR, CTR on top 3, conversions from search, latency p95, cost per 1k queries
- Duration: 4 weeks (2 weeks warmup + 2 weeks full analysis)

Next steps / asks for Shopline
- Confirm OK to run a 10% pilot starting the week of 2026-03-02.
- Confirm access for us to a small production-like sample (we requested 5k queries yesterday).
- Any privacy/legal constraints re: query logs retention — you mentioned a 30-day window; please confirm.

If that all looks good I’ll loop in Jonas to be the internal PM and Diego for the technical setup.

Best,
Marissa
--
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call: Shopline ranking pilot — model recommendations & A/B plan

Marissa / Emma — quick technical follow-up and concrete A/B plan draft.

High-level notes
- Model choices: redwood-rerank-1.0 is the lower-cost quantized variant (8-bit), roberta-crossenc-large-v2 gives slightly better quality but costs ~2x in GPU cycles. I recommend starting with redwood-rerank-1.0 for the 10% smoke test. If quality delta justifies cost we can switch to crossenc for the 50% rollout.

Proposed A/B test configuration (detailed)
- Traffic split: week 1–2: 10% variant, 90% control (sanity + instrumentation); week 3–4: 50/50 split for statistical power.
- Rescoring: run first-pass retrieval (top-200), truncate to top-50 for rerank (tradeoff: quality vs latency).
- Batching: use dynamic batching window (max 8ms or 16 requests) to optimize throughput on our Dedicated pool. Expect average batching factor of ~6 for peak hours.
- Instrumentation: add model_version tag, request_id, candidate-rank-before, candidate-rank-after, model_score fields to your analytics events. Keep separate logs for variant/control.
- Safety/QA: run a small manual eval set (200 queries with business-critical queries) and a judgment pass before bumping to 50%.

Expected signals and success criteria
- Primary: delta NDCG@10 >= +0.10 and MRR delta >= +0.10 vs baseline at 50% split.
- Secondary: +CTR(top3) and +conversion_rate from search > 2% (lift).
- Latency guardrail: variant p95 must remain <= 250ms overall; if exceeded, auto-fallback to control for that region/route.

Sensible rollout knobs
- Start with model_mode: "rerank-quantized"; keep "distil" ready as a warm fallback.
- Use feature-flagged rollout so we can instantly flip traffic back to control.

Attachments: ab_test_plan.md (detailed config; includes telemetry hooks) and pilot_config.yaml (sample deployment parameters).

Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa / Diego — thanks for the fast follow-up and the clear plan.

We’re interested in moving forward with the pilot. A few items from our side:
- Timeline: procurement needs an SOW and an indication of spend for the 4-week pilot. Can you provide a ballpark (we have an internal cap of $8k for pilots without extended approvals)?
- Data privacy: we confirm a 30-day retention window for query logs for pilot instrumentation. Please make sure PII is redacted and that logs are hashed before storage.
- Legal/Compliance: Samir (cc’d) will be our technical owner for the pilot. Procurement is copied for contracting.

Can you also provide the small manual eval set you mentioned (200 queries + labels) and an updated AB plan that calls out the guardrails we discussed? If we can get those by end of week (2026-02-26) procurement can sign off and we’ll target a pilot start of 2026-03-02.

Thanks — Emma
